THIS GIVES THE PLAYERS the feeling of purpose and reward rather than punish players with a massive qouta if they go above and beyond, OR make tickets used for items and MONEY used for permanant run upgrades like luck, more time, ect. Had a lot of fun and beat the game twice with friends. But the use of Gen AI was never disclosed, and I would not have made the purchase had it been. I'll use an example for my thinking here: If a vegan orders a veggie burger, they expect a veggie burger. If someone orders a dish that is pork free for religious reasons, they expect it to be pork free. When there is no mention of Gen AI usage on the Steam Store page, I expect the game to have been made WITHOUT the planet-killing theft-machine. For people who mention the price being low and that I had fun playing it... You simply don't get it. I would not have spent money on this had I known they used Gen AI. Period.

When I first heard the term "Friendslop", I was appalled and confused. Really? That sounds like something a sad and lonely person would say. It was such a poignant term that I couldn't help but think of it in the back of my mind, while playing Lethal Company, playing R.E.P.O, playing PEAK, et cetera. Still, I kept it on the backburner of silent ridicule within my mind. I was, after all, enjoying the games I was playing, even if they marketed on the same general trend. Gamble With Your Friends is the first game I have ever experienced where I couldn't help but relinquish my vocabulary to include this asinine word at the very tip of my tongue at every second of every minute I "played" this... product. It is nothing more, not to me, not to the developers, not to anybody. Utterly soulless, utterly mindless, and utterly substance-less. My only credit is that this game is exactly as advertised. You Gamble With Your Friends™! That's about it. You would think that a game centered about gambling would be right up my alley, given the fact that XCOM 2 is one of my favorite games ever. I call XCOM a "game" instead of a "product" because it requires a functioning cerebral cortex, largely opposed to Gamble With Your Friends, which was made to capitalize on the still remaining lobotomy victim population, and contains not but a few ways to slightly alter the house odds towards your favor. All you see in the trailer is the entire gameplay, other than a few little power-ups. This is all I have to say about the gameplay- because there is none. What about the other part? The part that takes up three-fourths of the game's title? The friends? Absolutely nothing changes gameplay-wise with friends. For the product itself, you may as well actually play it solo. Great, there are other little avatars in the room with you. There's also proximity chat, which ALSO adds absolutely nothing gameplay-wise, other than making it such that you can't even interact with some of your friends playing other games in other corners. Muting proximity chat and talking in discord subtracts absolutely nothing from the experience. It's not like you even have anything notable to talk about. "Oh, I won!" "Damn, I lost!" How exciting. If these few features add nothing to the game- why do they exist? It's because these features are part of some sort of checklist for these "friendslop" games, as if R.E.P.O, the main organ donor for this amalgamation, is some sort of divine bastion of game design. Proximity chat? Check. Object physics? Check. Tools to "le epically troll" your friends? Check. The particular item purchasing system? Snatched. There's even direct references to R.E.P.O and other games of similar caliber, as if it thinks it's part of the team. Who invited this guy? God, and the humor as well. I also used to find gambling jokes funny. Just 1.3 hours burned it out of me. This product reminds me of a band kid that has one (1) hit compared to a billion misses when it comes to his jokes. Instead of getting out while he was ahead, he instead decides to make it his entire personality. Interacting with this product is like listening to the Soviet Union anthem on the school bus on full blast. It also says "6 7" next to the bar. Isn't that funny, kids? We're tapped in too! It's entirely up to your friends to make you laugh, which can be accomplished without blowing up to eight dollars on this slop. There's also some allegations of AI usage when it came to developing this game. Most of the negative reviews seem to focus on that. I am not surprised. If anything, AI should have improved this game somehow. Make it suggest better gameplay or something. Instead, they made it create some ♥♥♥♥-ugly derivative art-style, most likely with other "friendslop" games mashed into its input. It took only an hour and twenty-two minutes to make me tired of looking at this. It doesn't even run well! How do you manage to poorly optimize THIS? The most amusement I have extracted from this game is found in a gloriously ironic statement made at the bottom of this Steam store page- "We’re TENSTACK -a small collective making creative, digestible games. A digestible game respects your money and time, is built around one strong idea, and doesn’t overstay its welcome. Our goal: games you can finish in a couple of sessions -without feeling stuffed". "Creative"? Hell no. "Respects your money and time"? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. See the run fail cutscene. "One strong idea"? Gambling with a house edge is a poor idea, not helped by a worse execution. "Doesn't overstay its welcome"? See the previous paragraph regarding the "band kid" allegory. Thank the lord that I can refund this thing, but it's regrettable that I don't get any reparations for wasted time. Nevertheless, the success of this product will only spawn more "friendslop", with what I'm sure will be with considerably less effort, which is actually saying a lot, since this game is not too far off of a skeleton. With that being said... I would like to announce a new indie title, "Watch Paint Dry With Your Friends"! It's currently in development and will be released when my ChatGPT message limit refreshes tomorrow. Patent pending.

I originally enjoyed this game a lot and looked forward to playing it with about 6 of my other friends in the future who all also had the game. However, now all of the friends who I had played with at some time (and myself as well) will not be playing this game due to the use of generative AI. I wish we could have gotten a disclaimer or any sort of transparency about the use of gen AI for assets in this game, but for now I don't think I'll be playing this game ever again if nothing changes, which is a real shame. In short, don't waste your money. I doubt this game has a long future with how things are going.

I usually don't have many issues with motion sickness in games (including VR), but I do with this game for some reason. So if you do easily get motion sick, I recommend you please skip this game (this may change in future). But if you really want to play this, just close your eyes when waking up at the start of the day (you may have to press random buttons on the keyboard to stand up) and tell your friends not to hit you with a baseball bat (as this was especially nauseating)! Also the option to turn off headbobbing doesn't make anything better because the headbobbing isn't the problem. Motion sickness aside! It's both funny and frustrating when you just meet the quota and then your friends decide to continue gambling because they're "on a streak" (clearly not responsible gamblers!). Though like others have already said, the gameplay loop does get very repetitive quickly and it lacks the dynamics of other co-op games to keep things relatively fresh. And because gambling games/machines are inherently random, this game is already at a disadvantage, as each time you gamble, nothing meaningful changes. Yes the games/machines rotate each in-game day and there are a few different levels of the casino (minimum spend changes), but ultimately you're pretty much doing the exact same thing every time (on later days it ends up coming down to just pressing spin on the machines heaps of times to try and win). Most of this review probably just seems like I am complaining about gambling and not the game itself, and yes you would be mostly right (it is not entirely the game's fault for not reinventing the wheel when it comes to gambling). Anyway, I spent way too long writing this review. If you like gambling then I'm sure this game will give you that surge of dopamine! For now, I can't recommend!

It's alright. I'm giving this a negative review because it needs more to be reccomended over other friendslop games in the field. It's charming at first and some of the humor gets a chuckle, but once you figure out how to rig a given casino game, there's very little to actually do, particularly later in the game when you realize that the floors aren't really any different from one another, they just give you bigger payouts. There needs to be more interactions beyond just, you win or lose at the end of the day. The trailer seems to imply the loan shark is a character you will interact with, and this is very much not the case. It would make the failure to clear a day more interesting if the loan shark did stuff like he did in the trailer (demanding the players mutilate themselves or eachother to continue), but there's none of that. You just restart. I also find that the body part removal system is pretty much a non-factor. Perhaps a "hardcore" mode where lost limbs can't be reattached would make the mechanic more impactful. The biggest problem, really, is that for a co-operative game there isn't really all that much co-operating you can actually do, because like an actual casino the games are mostly solo. If there were ways for players to coordinate to cheat, that might make things more interesting. Game's fine but it's a pretty big drag even by the end of the first playthrough because you're just doing the same thing again and again, or dying because your dimwit friend won't stop LETTING IT RIDE and wiping out an hour and a half of progress.

The game itself is relatively barebones, but incredibly hectic with a good group of friends. Giving an irresponsible friend group the power to gamble obscene amounts of money away strangely ends up being one of the most fun thrills you could have. In the few mechanics it offers and the various items you can obtain, there are surprisingly many different approaches to progressing in this game, with extra room for endless shenanigans. This game is also great for completionists, as the missions for each day can be rerolled and they're all pretty fun to achieve. The endings weren't as satisfying as I'd wished, but the journey of getting there is still a wild ride. Seriously, make the most fun you can out of this game, it's the most value you'll get out of it.
